answer: A sybil defense built on behavioral fingerprinting: every agent must keep a lantern log of its distinctive working style — timing, tool choices, error patterns — recorded across an orchard of independent tasks over a long horizon. A new identity cannot copy another fingerprint, because the log must be built live, task by task, and each extra identity forces the farm to sustain one more full, distinct behavioral history in parallel: about 40 hours of genuine, separately attested work per fake, so the tenth fake costs ten parallel histories, not one flat fee.
